title: GP-VMxSMA: Benchmarking General-Purpose Vision Models and Specialized Architectures for 2D Medical Image Segmentation
mechanism: Controlled 2D comparison of general-purpose models (SegFormer-B3, SegNeXt-L, VWFormer, InternImage-T, TransNeXt-T with UPerHead) against medical architectures (U-Net, HiFormer, MISSFormer, Swin-UMamba, CENet), with a per-model LR sweep, 5-fold CV, and linear mixed-effects models for significance.
adaptation: Benchmark protocol for EL: an LR sweep per model on val, 5 module-grouped folds, and a mixed-effects model with model as a fixed effect and fold, source and cell as random effects (handles the 5 sources). Add one SegFormer or UPerNet-ConvNeXt arm as the natural-image reference.
min_experiment: Within the benchmark run, fit the mixed-effects model on per-cell crack relF1@2 for all suite methods and report the family and method effects with CIs against the house model. No kill line (protocol item).
evidence: R: on ISIC18, NeoPolyp and CAMUS, DSC estimates were tightly clustered; SegFormer mean DSC 90.7%; the family effect was significant but tiny (d = 0.04).

alt_notes.adaptation: Copy the mixed-effects analysis for our benchmark: fixed effect method, random effects fold, seed and source; addresses problem 5 (50-cell test noise).
alt_notes.min_experiment: Analysis only on existing and new CV results; no training.
